notes: Reviewed and kept unchanged in structure: every s001–s017 and t001–t026 appears in exactly one unit, all heads are members of their arrays, and the two unrepresented units are source-only with null target heads.

The one materially contested unit, ἀπείραστός ἐστιν → *cannot be tempted*, is now decided on a named precedent rather than on the general argument the accepted note gave: rule 64's `μήτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ χριστός;` → *Can this be the Christ?* has the same modal-plus-*be* shape and gives the modal to the other token while the expressed ἐστιν keeps *be*. That confirms the accepted split (*cannot* + *tempted* on the adjective, *be* on the copula) against the whole-phrase reading that would leave ἐστιν unrepresented; both notes now carry the cross-reference.
*cannot* is a single solid word, so rule 39 bars splitting it, and the privative negation in it is the adjective's — which is why the modal cannot be handed to ἐστιν instead.

Heads checked apart from edges: lexical verbs over auxiliaries and over the finite-looking *Let* (rules 9, 17, 73), the negative indefinites on *no* rather than the supplied *man* (rule 69's explicit heading of *any man* on *any*), and κακῶν on *evil* with the case preposition riding along.

s016 αὐτός → *he himself* is the only other place a different analysis is available: *he* could be read as πειράζει's rule 9 subject with only *himself* on the pronoun. Kept whole because the emphatic needs the subject word to attach to, and the alternative head is recorded in the unit note.

s008: the article before θεός is unrepresented because the ASV supplies no determiner of any kind — not *the*, not *a*, not a demonstrative — so rules 51 and 60 are not in play and rule 23 decides it.
